analysis.subject: finance
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains saving early for college costs, how compound interest grows money over time, how to use an online calculator with initial investment and rates, and defines key terms for post-secondary saving.

overview.headline: Earlier saving lets compound interest grow money for education costs over time

keyPoints.point: Compound interest earns interest on both saved money and earned interest
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

keyPoints.point: Saving early in an account that pays interest helps money grow faster
keyPoints.quote: The sooner you start saving in an account that pays interest, the faster your money can grow.

keyPoints.point: Students explore growth over time using an online compound interest calculator
keyPoints.quote: Students use an online compound interest calculator to explore the value of saving money over time for future education goals.

keyPoints.point: Post-secondary schooling after high school includes forms beyond just college
keyPoints.quote: Post-secondary education: Includes all forms of schooling after high school, not just college.

keyTerms.gloss: interest earned on saved money plus previously earned interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

keyTerms.gloss: percentage charged for borrowed money or paid for deposited money
keyTerms.quote: Interest rate: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant for letting you use its money.

keyTerms.gloss: initial amount you invest that earns interest over time
keyTerms.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).

keyTerms.gloss: all forms of schooling after high school beyond just college
keyTerms.quote: Post-secondary education: Includes all forms of schooling after high school, not just college.

keyTerms.gloss: something you spend money on that you expect will earn a financial return
keyTerms.quote: Investment: Something you spend your money on that you expect will earn a financial return.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Worked example shows principal plus earned interest growth with rate and frequency to illustrate starting early
componentPlan.focusQuote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Vocabulary definitions for interest and saving provide checkable facts for college saving decisions
componentPlan.focusQuote: Interest rate: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant for letting you use its money.
